method: Stock v11 TimeSeries, same unmodified O1 binary. Source-specified stale-NaN bit check only, original TAGS/SAMPLES, no new index. Tiny six-series synthetic fixture with multi-INSERT/duplicate max arbitration. Native single prometheusQueryRange over five 60s evaluation grid ticks compared with one SQL statement CROSS JOIN same five ticks, avg per full-ID after filtering exact stale-bit values and then avg by(stage). Explicit isNaN and finite surrogate ensure original NaNs are retained and JSON can express their classification.
math_and_semantics: Native range selector excludes exact bit payload 0x7ff0000000000002, preserves ordinary NaN 0x7ff8000000000001. The SQL WHERE bit filter is equivalent for this verified subset; filtering all NaNs is invalid.
22 exact nonempty stage/timestamp/value-or-NaN-classification observations matched across native vs stale-safe SQL in a five-tick single query.
The earlier unfiltered SQL differed at six entries, including 2 stale_mix query ticks and 4 stale_only spurious series ticks.
Input same-timestamp 1 vs7 wins 7 after TimeSeriesSink dedup, with cross-INSERT time duplicate also merged into two stored points; standard window (start,end] respected.
No sidecar, planner patch, new C++ compile, production data or image changes.
limits: Finite/stale/ordinary-NaN and duplicate tiny fixture only; no histograms, rate, regex/ACL, arbitrary PromQL operators or multi-client throughput.
One pinned O1 binary and tiny 5-tick exactness test, not speed. Stale-safe bit filter CPU cost will be measured in a separate frozen 2.488m R01 ABBA.
